Mapping NHANES PAM quality flags

Source: vignettes/nhanes-pam-flags.Rmd
nhanes-pam-flags.Rmd
library(actibase)

Scope

CDC NHANES PAM quality flags are reported at the minute level. Most actibase detectors operate on raw samples, so the table identifies the closest function and its output, along with parameters and known differences. These helpers are general-purpose; CDC-specific thresholds below are example settings for reproducing the NHANES rules.

CDC code mapping

CDC code CDC definition (summary) actibase function and output Match notes
A–C Axis-specific spikes: adjacent-sample change ≥11 g acti_flag_spike(by_axis = TRUE): flag_spike_X/Y/Z Sample-level; set spike_size = 11.
D–F Per-minute count of positive near-limit values, ≥690 samples acti_flag_device_limit_windows(): flag_device_max_X/Y/Z Set min_count = 690, window_seconds = 60, range ±6 g, and epsilon = 0.05.
G–I Per-minute count of negative near-limit values, ≥690 samples acti_flag_device_limit_windows(): flag_device_min_X/Y/Z Same thresholds as D–F, for negative values.
J–L Contiguous positive near-limit run, ≥160 samples acti_flag_contiguous_device_limits(): flag_contiguous_max_X/Y/Z Set min_length = 160; CDC assigns the run to every overlapping minute.
M–O Contiguous negative near-limit run, ≥160 samples acti_flag_contiguous_device_limits(): flag_contiguous_min_X/Y/Z Set min_length = 160; CDC permits runs to cross minute boundaries.
P Contiguous impossible gravity values acti_flag_impossible(): flag_impossible CDC settings: seven samples, <0.01 g change on each axis, vector magnitude >1.25 g, excluding ±6 g values.
Q Contiguous adjacent zero values acti_flag_all_zero(): flag_all_zero Package checks all three axes. CDC documents a historical programming error that checked only X; exact reproduction of that error is not intended.
R Contiguous identical, non-zero three-axis samples acti_flag_repeated_samples(): flag_repeated_samples Use min_length = 2, exclude_zero = TRUE, require_equal_axes = TRUE. CDC run lengths and minute attribution may differ.
S–U Axis-specific 1-second spike counts acti_flag_spike_second(by_axis = TRUE): flag_spike_second_X/Y/Z Set window_seconds = 1, min_spikes = 13, spike_size = 11; CDC counts qualifying local-extremum events.
V Minute before and after an invalid minute acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods(): flag_adjacent_invalid Caller supplies invalid periods. Match CDC’s hour-boundary exception with the group argument.
W–Y Axis-specific interval jumps within a second acti_flag_interval_jump(by_axis = TRUE): flag_interval_jump_X/Y/Z Set window_seconds = 1, min_repeats = 10, min_distinct = 3, min_separation = 0.5; this is an approximation.

The CDC summary describes the 690-sample positive and negative limits as occurring in a minute, and the contiguous flags as runs of at least 160 samples. At 80 Hz, these correspond to about 8.6 seconds and 2 seconds, respectively. Minute boundaries and CDC’s separate raw-data flagging workflow can affect direct comparisons.

Producing letter labels

acti_flag_cdc_labels() maps logical flag columns already in a data frame to CDC letter codes. It does not run detectors. For axis-specific codes, create axis-specific outputs first (using by_axis = TRUE where available):

raw <- acti_flag_spike(raw, by_axis = TRUE)
raw <- acti_flag_device_limit_windows(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                      min_count = 690)
raw <- acti_flag_contiguous_device_limits(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                          min_length = 160)
raw <- acti_flag_cdc_labels(raw)

By default, the result is stored in PAXFLGSM, with multiple letters concatenated alphabetically (for example, "ABP"). Rows with no true mapped flags receive an empty string. You can provide a custom named flag_map when your columns use different names.

Reference

Definitions and the documented caveats about the historical Q flag and contiguous-run reporting come from the CDC NHANES PAM Data Quality Flag Summary Table.
